subject.title: Rebrand text-substitution filter on tool-call arguments silently misroutes file ops

question: Should output text transforms continue to rewrite structured tool-call arguments by default, or should path/file-operation strings be exempted or handled by a path-aware policy?
rationale: The current behavior is both a documented Plugin SDK capability for placeholder/privacy restoration and the mechanism that can misroute filesystem operations, so automation cannot choose the permanent compatibility boundary safely.

options.title: Add path-aware tool-argument safety
options.body: Preserve output transforms for non-path tool arguments, but skip or constrain replacements in path/file-operation contexts and validate the behavior with dual-directory proof.

options.title: Disable all tool-argument transforms
options.body: Stop applying output replacements to structured tool-call arguments, avoiding path misrouting but breaking documented placeholder restoration use cases.

options.title: Keep current behavior and document policy
options.body: Leave tool-argument transforms as-is and require plugins to avoid path-affecting replacements or use dedicated hooks, accepting the reported misrouting risk.

recommendation.title: Add path-aware tool-argument safety
recommendation.body: Preserve output transforms for non-path tool arguments, but skip or constrain replacements in path/file-operation contexts and validate the behavior with dual-directory proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter introduced the text-transform surface and is directly connected to the core Plugin SDK compatibility behavior that needs a boundary decision.
